clue.text: Headwear's better with uniform

parts.note: a flat rate or flat fee is uniform, the same for everyone
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A boast that hats are improved by matching a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Headwear stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat cap is a soft peaked cloth hat, a classic item of British headwear.

clue.text: High value letter put alongside tees in Scrabble?

indicators.note: Scrabble is played by shuffling lettered tiles, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: em is the spelt-out name of the letter M

explanation.surface: A Scrabble player puts a high-scoring tile next to the tees on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Scrabble' scrambles TEES to ESTE; the letter EM goes alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is the high regard or value in which something is held; a noun synonym.

clue.text: Gadget peripherally used during cooking regime?

definitions.text: Gadget peripherally used during cooking regime?

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the time, and so the letters, of the other
cooking suggests the letters are being worked up into something new
peripherally points to the outermost letters of the word Gadget

explanation.surface: A kitchen device brought into play while following a cooking routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' makes EGIMER; read whole, the clue also describes the device itself, so the definition is the entire clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg timer is a small kitchen gadget used to time boiling eggs, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Ships today active in French sea

indicators.note: in says the next two pieces go inside the French word

parts.note: mer is French for sea
now means at the present time, today
A is the grammatical abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: Ships currently operating in French waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Men-of-war are armed sailing warships, so they are a kind of ship.

clue.text: Carnivore taking head off rats etc with minimum of effort

indicators.note: taking the head off means removing the first letter of the word for pests

parts.note: vermin are rats and similar pests

indicators.note: the minimum of effort is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A predator easily decapitating rats and other pests.
explanation.definitionFit: The ermine, a stoat in its white winter coat, is a small meat-eating mammal.

clue.text: Notice retired male staff placed back to back

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the following pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Des is a man's name, short for Desmond
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A notice about retired male employees, seated back to back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns DESROD backwards into DORSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Addorsed is a heraldic term for two figures shown turned back to back.

clue.text: In addition to running surgery, upper-class type mostly travels around

parts.note: a machine that is on is running

indicators.note: travels around says one piece goes round the other
mostly means dropping the last letter

parts.note: a toff is a posh, upper-class person
op is short for operation, surgery

explanation.surface: Besides running a surgery, a posh person keeps travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for a posh person; 'mostly' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means besides or as well as, a direct idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Dish with beef perhaps Neal spilt around sink

indicators.note: around says the scrambled name goes round the other piece
spilt suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: to sag is to sink or droop

explanation.surface: Neal drops a beef dish around the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' makes LANE, which opens up to hold the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked pasta dish, commonly layered with minced beef.

clue.text: Type of boot makes loud noise disturbing doctor

indicators.note: disturbing here means breaking into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to doctor is to rig or falsify
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A boot that clatters noisily and bothers the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding boots are tall boots worn on horseback, one kind of boot.

clue.text: Somerset community elder perhaps occupies empty seat

indicators.note: occupies says one piece fills the space inside the other
empty means the word seat with its middle letters removed

parts.note: the elder is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: A senior villager in Somerset takes a vacant seat.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is a county in south-west England; Street is a village there. 'elder' tempts as an old person but is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Street is a real village in Somerset, home of the Clarks shoe firm, so a community there.

clue.text: Womble circles, collecting rubbish primarily in front third of Common

indicators.note: collecting says the circles gather the next pieces inside them

parts.note: two circles look like two O's

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word rubbish
the front third of a six-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A Womble gathers litter on Wimbledon Common.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wombles are British children's TV characters who tidy Wimbledon Common; Orinoco is one of them. 'front third of' takes CO, the first two of Common's six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Orinoco is the name of one of the Wombles, so he is an example of a Womble.

clue.text: Relative twice joined Tina, regularly selecting Abba song

indicators.note: twice says the relative's word appears two times

parts.note: mam is a dialect word for mother, a relative

indicators.note: regularly selecting takes every other letter of the name

explanation.surface: A relative and Tina team up to pick an Abba number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly selecting' takes I and A from Tina.
explanation.definitionFit: Mamma Mia is a 1975 hit single by the Swedish pop group Abba.

clue.text: No time to meet girl around railway station

indicators.note: around here means turned round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: No time for a date with a girl near the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns NOTSUE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is a major London railway terminus serving the West Coast Main Line.

clue.text: Water source soldier's not required

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring, a source of water
RE is the Royal Engineers, so a soldier from that corps

explanation.surface: A soldier's spring water turns out to be surplus to needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after soldier stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare means surplus or extra, things not needed for the moment.

clue.text: Old musician's sandwiches have extremely appetising filling

indicators.note: filling says the extreme letters go inside, like the filling of a sandwich

parts.note: panini are Italian toasted sandwiches

indicators.note: extremely picks the outermost letters of the word appetising

explanation.surface: An old performer's sandwiches have a delicious filling.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after musician stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was a 19th-century Italian violin virtuoso, a musician of the past.

clue.text: Loo duly vacated, revealing drug

parts.note: can is American slang for a toilet, a loo

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A toilet duly cleared reveals hidden narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is street slang for various drugs, especially cocaine or ecstasy.

clue.text: Whiff nuts and lemons

parts.note: a whiff is a breath of air
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A smell of nuts and lemons.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemons is slang for fools or dimwits, which is what airheads are.

clue.text: One helps budding graduate after terraced property in edges of Goring

indicators.note: in says the next pieces sit inside the outer letters
edges of picks the first and last letters of the word Goring
after places the graduate following the terrace

parts.note: a row is a terrace of houses
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate living in a Goring terrace helps out.
explanation.walkthrough: A growbag is a plastic sack of compost that plants are grown in. Goring is an English village.
explanation.definitionFit: A growbag is a compost-filled bag for growing plants, so something that helps budding plants.

clue.text: Wave at nursing students northbound on motorway

indicators.note: in a down entry northbound means read upwards, so backwards
nursing means holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students
the M1 is a British motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: Waving at nursing students heading north on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: AT holding NUS gives ANUST; 'northbound' turns it to TSUNA. The M1 is London's main motorway north.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave set off by an earthquake.

clue.text: Oscar runs through Latin, randomly being tested

parts.note: Oscar is O in the phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: through says one piece passes inside the other
randomly says the letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Oscar dashes through Latin, tested at random.
explanation.walkthrough: R inside LATIN gives a pool that 'randomly' rearranges to NTRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on trial is undergoing a test, as a product on trial is being tried out.

clue.text: Black wig one's half-exposed somewhere in Belgium

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
rug is slang for a wig

indicators.note: half-exposed means stripped of half its letters, the first half here

explanation.surface: A black wig half-revealed somewhere in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-exposed' strips ON from ONES, leaving ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruges is a medieval canal city in Belgium's Flanders region, so a place there.

clue.text: Heavenly body modelled to make money, we hear

parts.note: an artist's model sat for the portrait

indicators.note: we hear says the next word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to earn is to make money

explanation.surface: A celestial body sculpted to turn a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the ringed sixth planet from the Sun, a heavenly body.

clue.text: Competition's boring without English RU team

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sans means without
a race is a competition

explanation.surface: A rugby match is dull without the English side.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Competition stands for 'is'. RU means Rugby Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracens are a professional rugby union club based in north London.

clue.text: Character from Argos impregnates party hen

indicators.note: impregnates means gets inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a political party
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character used in the Greek city of Argos

explanation.surface: A character from the catalogue shop Argos gets a party hen pregnant.
explanation.walkthrough: Argos is both a Greek city and a British catalogue store, steering away from the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cochin is a large domestic chicken breed with feathered legs, so a kind of hen.

clue.text: Succeed with poser, essentially having to name Orwell character

parts.note: to win is to succeed

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so the central letter of poser

explanation.surface: Winning a puzzle earns the right to name a character from Orwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Smith is the protagonist of George Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Royal husband given reminder about card game

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
a cue is a prompt or reminder

explanation.surface: A royal husband is reminded about a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ERHCUE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Euchre is a trick-taking card game for four players, popular in North America.

clue.text: Much of Roman emperor seen on bronze coin from the past

indicators.note: seen on places the emperor piece after the colour, as on reads in an across entry

parts.note: tan is a bronze-like brown colour

indicators.note: much of means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: An emperor's head on an old bronze coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was an old British sixpence coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanner was slang for the pre-decimal British sixpence, a coin no longer in use.

clue.text: On reflection, varied amount when cutting cake

indicators.note: On reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
cutting says the answer slices through these words, hidden in them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Thinking back, cake portions varied when it was sliced.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'when cutting cake' as the definition; 'when cutting' is the hidden-word signal and only 'cake' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a plain sponge cake, traditionally served with Madeira wine.
